prompt_context:
PAPER: Zemlevskiy 2024, arXiv:2411.02486 (OSTI 2878986)
"Scalable Quantum Simulations of Scattering in Scalar Field Theory on 120 Qubits"
IBM Heron ibm_fez, 120 qubits, digitized (nq=2) lattice phi^4 theory, m=1/2, lambda in {0,2},
wavepackets at k=+-pi/3, sigma_k=pi/3, time evolution t=1..9.

CLAIMS TESTED IN THIS INDEPENDENT REPLICATION:
  C1 Vacuum <phi^2> is translation-invariant (should be uniform across sites).
  C2 Interacting vacuum has smaller <phi^2> than free (correlation length shorter).
  C3 Free-theory dispersion E_k = sqrt(m^2 + 4 sin^2(k/2)) [paper Eq. 2].
  C4 Collision-peak amplitude is smaller for lambda=2 than lambda=0 (Fig. 11).
  C5 Interacting collision peak arrives later in time (Fig. 11 says ~t=5 vs t=4).

METHOD: Built the paper's digitized JLP-basis Hamiltonian (Eqs. 1, 13-16) exactly
for L=8 (Hilbert dim 4^8 = 65,536). Used scipy sparse Lanczos for the vacuum and
scipy.sparse.linalg.expm_multiply for time evolution. The two-wavepacket state was
NOT the paper's variational SC-ADAPT-VQE circuit (which requires qiskit + classical
optimization on their choice of ansatz parameters we don't have) but a simple
smeared phi_j Gaussian excitation of |vac> with the paper's momenta k_0 = +-pi/3
and Gaussian envelope width in x-space. Everything else follows the paper exactly.

RESULTS (from claim_verdicts.json):

C1: vacuum <phi^2> uniformity
  lambda=0: mean = 0.416468, std/mean = 3.75e-15
  lambda=2: mean = 0.359611, std/mean = 4.63e-16
  (both std < 1e-15 of mean — translation-invariant to machine precision)

C2: interacting vacuum has smaller <phi^2>
  ratio int/free = 0.8635   (< 1 as paper expects)

C3: dispersion E_k
  Numerical evaluation of Eq. 2 matches the closed form to 1e-10 for every k in the BZ.

C4: collision peak, lambda=0 vs lambda=2
  Peak amplitudes at t=1..9 (free / int):
    free = ['0.201', '0.461', '0.749', '0.481', '0.264', '0.279', '0.343', '0.200', '0.367']
    int  = ['0.124', '0.403', '0.472', '0.314', '0.405', '0.297', '0.180', '0.246', '0.227']
  Average ratio int/free = 0.845 < 1  (interaction attenuates the peak)

C5: time delay
  Global peak time free: t = 3.0
  Global peak time int:  t = 3.0
  Delta_t = 0.0
  Paper Fig 11 says delay ~ +1 (free peaks at t~4, interacting at t~5).
  Our finding: NO delay at L=8 (both peak at t=3). This is very likely a finite-size
  artifact (L=8 with PBCs on a ring means the wavepackets separate by only 4 sites
  before wrapping around, so the "collision" is confounded with self-recollision).
  The paper uses L=60.

RESOURCE / CIRCUIT SPOT-CHECK (not physically verified, just consistency-read):
  Paper Table II: 4924 two-qubit gates, depth 103 for t=7-9. Each time step adds
  22*ceil(t/3) to depth (paper text). For t=7-9: 22*3 = 66 additional depth on top
  of vacuum prep (25) + wavepacket prep (14). Sum = 66+25+14 = 105, which is
  consistent within one gate-cancellation slot with the reported 103. (Cannot
  verify gate COUNT without reconstructing the actual circuits.)

VERDICT VOCABULARY: REPLICATED / PARTIAL / SPOT-CHECK / NO-GO / CONTRADICTED /
BLOCKED / FAILED.

Please output a JSON object of the form:
  {
    "verdict": "PARTIAL",             # one of the above
    "confidence": 0.0-1.0,
    "coverage_note": "which claims tested vs total testable",
    "agreement_note": "quantitative agreement quality",
    "one_line": "one-sentence bottom line"
  }
Only output the JSON. No preface.
